request: Make the tally CLI simple to use. New users get lost. It belongs under Feature #70 (Getting started).

exchanges.say: You want tally to be simple for new users. Today it has 6 commands and 27 flags (command:tally); `tally add` needs 3 required flags and fails until you run `tally init` (command:tally add, README). Four questions, riskiest first.

questions.ask: What do new users type first? Today `tally add` needs `tally init` first and fails without ~/.tally/config.toml (README). Should the first add just work?
questions.default: The first `tally add` creates what it needs, because a required setup step is where new users get lost.

questions.ask: `tally add` has 7 flags today and requires --amount, --category, and --date (command:tally add). Which task should be simple, and which flags must stay required?
questions.default: Adding an expense, with the amount and category as plain words and every flag optional.

questions.ask: When a command fails today it prints `tally: missing required flag` with no hint. What should it say?
questions.default: The cause and the exact command to type instead.

questions.ask: There is no help screen beyond a one-line usage. Should `tally --help` fit one screen (24 lines) with an example?
questions.default: Usage, the commonest commands, and one example, in 24 lines.

answers.text: The first thing people type is `tally add 12.50 lunch`, and it fails because they never ran `tally init`. It should just work: create what it needs on first use, in GBP like `tally init` does today.
Adding an expense is the task. `tally add` should take the amount and a category as plain words, with every flag optional.
When something is wrong it should say what to type instead.
Yes, one screen, 24 lines is fine, with an example of add.

exchanges.say: So: the first `tally add 12.50 lunch` just works, the amount and category are plain words, errors say what to type, and help fits one screen. Two more.

questions.ask: Exit codes: every failure exits 1 today. Use 2 for a usage mistake, like a missing amount?
questions.default: 2 for usage errors, 1 for the rest.

questions.ask: Should tally remember anything new, such as the last category?
Six commands and 27 flags in all (command:tally). Worth dropping report and export to make it simpler?

answers.text: That is not part of what I asked for; park it.

exchanges.say: Here is what done looks like. Goal: someone who just installed tally logs their first expense without reading anything. Done when: on a fresh machine `tally add 12.50 lunch` exits 0 and `tally list` shows it in GBP; `tally add` has 0 required flags and takes the amount and category as words; `tally add` with nothing exits 2 and shows the example to type; and `tally --help` fits 24 lines with that example. Dropping report and export is parked.
